p0.original: The stock which is lent at interest is always considered as a capital by the lender. He expects that in due time it is to be restored to him, and that, in the mean time, the borrower is to pay him a certain annual rent for the use of it. The borrower may use it either as a capital, or as a stock reserved for immediate consumption. If he uses it as a capital, he employs it in the maintenance of productive labourers, who reproduce the value, with a profit. He can, in this case, both restore the capital, and pay the interest, without alienating or encroaching upon any other source of revenue. If he uses it as a stock reserved for immediate consumption, he acts the part of a prodigal, and dissipates, in the maintenance of the idle, what was destined for the support of the industrious. He can, in this case, neither restore the capital nor pay the interest, without either alienating or encroaching upon some other source of revenue, such as the property or the rent of land.
p0.zh: 出贷人总是将利息出借的股票视为资本。 他期望在适当的时候恢复到他身上,在那个刻薄的时间里,借款人要付给他一定的年租,用于使用.借款人可以将其用作资本,也可以作为储备供即时消费的股票. 若用之为资本,则用之为维持有产之工,以再生之值,以利为用. 在这种情况下,他既可以恢复资本,又可以支付利息,而不能疏远或侵占任何其他收入来源。 如果他把它作为供立即消费的股票,他就扮演浪人的角色,并消散了闲人的维持,什么是注定要支持勤劳者的. 在这种情况下,他既不能恢复资本,也不能支付利息,而不能疏远或侵占其他一些收入来源,如财产或土地租金。

p1.original: The stock which is lent at interest is, no doubt, occasionally employed in both these ways, but in the former much more frequently than in the latter. The man who borrows in order to spend will soon be ruined, and he who lends to him will generally have occasion to repent of his folly. To borrow or to lend for such a purpose, therefore, is, in all cases, where gross usury is out of the question, contrary to the interest of both parties; and though it no doubt happens sometimes, that people do both the one and the other, yet, from the regard that all men have for their own interest, we may be assured, that it cannot happen so very frequently as we are sometimes apt to imagine. Ask any rich man of common prudence, to which of the two sorts of people he has lent the greater part of his stock, to those who he thinks will employ it profitably, or to those who will spend it idly, and he will laugh at you for proposing the question. Even among borrowers, therefore, not the people in the world most famous for frugality, the number of the frugal and industrious surpasses considerably that of the prodigal and idle.
p1.zh: 毫无疑问,借入利息的股票有时以这两种方式使用,但前者比后者频繁得多。借人以资者,不久必废;借人以资者,一般有悔其愚. 因此,为此目的借贷或借贷,在所有情况下,都与双方的利益相反,总的利息都不存在;尽管毫无疑问有时会发生,但人们既会这样做,也会这样做,然而,从所有人为自己的利益着想来看,我们可以保证,这种情况不可能像我们有时能够想象的那样频繁发生。问任何富人,凡有共同谨慎,他借给哪一种人,他把股的较大部分,借给谁,他以为会用它来赚钱,或者随便花的人,他嘲笑你提出这个问题. 因此,即使在借款人中,世界上最以节俭而闻名的人,节俭和勤俭的人数也大大超过了浪子和闲置的人数。

p2.original: The only people to whom stock is commonly lent, without their being expected to make any very profitable use of it, are country gentlemen, who borrow upon mortgage. Even they scarce ever borrow merely to spend. What they borrow, one may say, is commonly spent before they borrow it. They have generally consumed so great a quantity of goods, advanced to them upon credit by shop-keepers and tradesmen, that they find it necessary to borrow at interest, in order to pay the debt. The capital borrowed replaces the capitals of those shop-keepers and tradesmen which the country gentlemen could not have replaced from the rents of their estates. It is not properly borrowed in order to be spent, but in order to replace a capital which had been spent before.
p2.zh: 只有乡绅们通过抵押贷款借贷,而他们却得不到任何利润。 甚至连他们都很少借钱去花 他们借的东西,可以说,通常是在他们借之前就用完的。 他们通常消耗大量货物,经店主和商人信贷后预支给他们,以致于他们认为必须按利息借贷,以偿还债务。所借资本取代了那些店主和商人的首都,而乡绅们却无法从他们的庄园租金中取代这些首都.其借款不适当,以待支用,而以取代以前支用过的资本.

p3.original: Almost all loans at interest are made in money, either of paper, or of gold and silver; but what the borrower really wants, and what the lender readily supplies him with, is not the money, but the money's worth, or the goods which it can purchase. If he wants it as a stock for immediate consumption, it is those goods only which he can place in that stock. If he wants it as a capital for employing industry, it is from those goods only that the industrious can be furnished with the tools, materials, and maintenance necessary for carrying on their work. By means of the loan, the lender, as it were, assigns to the borrower his right to a certain portion of the annual produce of the land and labour of the country, to be employed as the borrower pleases.
p3.zh: 几乎所有的利息贷款都是用钱,或者用纸,或者用金银;但是借款人真正想要的,以及贷款人随时提供给他的东西,并不是钱,而是钱的价值,或者它可以购买的商品. 如果他想要它作为库存 立即消费, 这是那些商品,只有他可以放入该库存。 如果他想把它作为雇用工业的资本,那么只有从这些商品中才能为勤奋者提供他们从事工作所必需的工具、材料和维护。 通过贷款,贷款人按原样向借款人转让其取得国家土地年产和劳务的一定部分的权利,作为借款人随意雇用.

p4.original: The quantity of stock, therefore, or, as it is commonly expressed, of money, which can be lent at interest in any country, is not regulated by the value of the money, whether paper or coin, which serves as the instrument of the different loans made in that country, but by the value of that part of the annual produce, which, as soon as it comes either from the ground, or from the hands of the productive labourers, is destined, not only for replacing a capital, but such a capital as the owner does not care to be at the trouble of employing himself. As such capitals are commonly lent out and paid back in money, they constitute what is called the monied interest. It is distinct, not only from the landed, but from the trading and manufacturing interests, as in these last the owners themselves employ their own capitals. Even in the monied interest, however, the money is, as it were, but the deed of assignment, which conveys from one hand to another those capitals which the owners do not care to employ themselves. Those capitals may be greater, in almost any proportion, than the amount of the money which serves as the instrument of their conveyance; the same pieces of money successively serving for many different loans, as well as for many different purchases. A, for example, lends to W £1000, with which W immediately purchases of B £1000 worth of goods. B having no occasion for the money himself, lends the identical pieces to X, with which X immediately purchases of C another £1000 worth of goods. C, in the same manner, and for the same reason, lends them to Y, who again purchases goods with them of D. In this manner, the same pieces, either of coin or of paper, may, in the course of a few days, serve as the Instrument of three different loans, and of three different purchases, each of which is, in value, equal to the whole amount of those pieces. What the three monied men, A, B, and C, assigned to the three borrowers, W, X, and Y, is the power of making those purchases. In this power consist both the value and the use of the loans. The stock lent by the three monied men is equal to the value of the goods which can be purchased with it, and is three times greater than that of the money with which the purchases are made. Those loans, however, may be all perfectly well secured, the goods purchased by the different debtors being so employed as, in due time, to bring back, with a profit, an equal value either of coin or of paper. And as the same pieces of money can thus serve as the instrument of different loans to three, or, for the same reason, to thirty times their value, so they may likewise successively serve as the instrument of repayment.
p4.zh: 因此,库存的数量,或通常表示的,可以借给任何国家利息的货币的数量,不受货币价值的制约,无论是纸币还是硬币,货币价值是该国不同贷款的工具,而是受年产的这一部分价值的制约,一旦来自地面,或来自生产劳工的手中,这些价值就注定了,不仅是为了更换资本,而且像所有者这样的资本也不在乎自己在用工上遇到麻烦. 由于这些首都通常被借出并用钱还款,它们构成了所谓的 " 欠债利息 " 。 它不仅与土地不同,也与贸易和制造业利益不同,因为最后这些业主自己雇用自己的首都。 然而,即使为了利息,这笔钱也照原样是转让契约,它从一手传递给另一手,使那些所有者不关心自己雇用的首都。 这些首都几乎在任何比例上都可能大于作为运送工具的货币数额;同样的货币相继用于许多不同的贷款,以及许多不同的采购。 例如,A向W1000英镑借出,W随即购买价值B1000英镑的商品.B本人没有机会获得这笔钱,将相同的物品借给X,X立即用它再购买价值1000英镑的C.丙,以同样的方式,也出于同样的原因,借给Y,Y再次与他们一起购买D类商品. 这样一来,同一枚硬币或纸币,在几天内,可以作为三种不同贷款的票据,以及三种不同购买的票据,每一种价值相当于这些硬币的全部金额.三个修道院的人,A,B,C, 分配给三个借款人,W,X,和Y, 是这些购买的力量。 这种权力包括贷款的价值和使用。三个寺主所借的股票等于可以与之购买的商品的价值,是购买时所借货币的三倍。 但是,这些贷款可能都完全有保障,不同债务人购买的货物在适当的时候被雇用,以便以利润带回硬币或纸币的同等价值。 由于同一笔钱可以因此作为三种不同贷款的工具,或出于同样的原因,作为价值的三十倍,因此它们也可以相继作为还款工具。

p5.original: A capital lent at interest may, in this manner, be considered as an assignment, from the lender to the borrower, of a certain considerable portion of the annual produce, upon condition that the burrower in return shall, during the continuance of the loan, annually assign to the lender a small portion, called the interest; and, at the end of it, a portion equally considerable with that which had originally been assigned to him, called the repayment. Though money, either coin or paper, serves generally as the deed of assignment, both to the smaller and to the more considerable portion, it is itself altogether different from what is assigned by it.
p5.zh: 以这种方式出借的利息资本,可被视为贷款人向借款人转让相当大一部分年度产品,条件是作为回报的挖井人应在继续贷款期间每年向贷款人转让一小部分利息,称为利息;在贷款结束时,与原先分配给他的部分相当大的部分称为还款。 虽然钱财,无论是硬币还是纸币,一般都作为转让的契约,无论是对较小的还是对相当大的一部分,但钱本身与它所分配的东西完全不同。

p6.original: In proportion as that share of the annual produce which, as soon as it comes either from the ground, or from the hands of the productive labourers, is destined for replacing a capital, increases in any country, what is called the monied interest naturally increases with it. The increase of those particular capitals from which the owners wish to derive a revenue, without being at the trouble of employing them themselves, naturally accompanies the general increase of capitals; or, in other words, as stock increases, the quantity of stock to be lent at interest grows gradually greater and greater.
p6.zh: 与年产中一旦来自地面或来自生产性工人手中的、注定要取代资本的份额成比例,在任何国家都有所增加,所谓不偿利息自然会随之增加。拥有者希望从中获取收入,而无需自己雇用这些收入的特定首都的增加,自然伴随着首都的普遍增加;换言之,随着库存的增加,利息贷款的数量也逐渐增加。

p7.original: As the quantity of stock to be lent at interest increases, the interest, or the price which must be paid for the use of that stock, necessarily diminishes, not only from those general causes which make the market price of things commonly diminish as their quantity increases, but from other causes which are peculiar to this particular case. As capitals increase in any country, the profits which can be made by employing them necessarily diminish. It becomes gradually more and more difficult to find within the country a profitable method of employing any new capital. There arises, in consequence, a competition between different capitals, the owner of one endeavouring to get possession of that employment which is occupied by another; but, upon most occasions, he can hope to justle that other out of this employment by no other means but by dealing upon more reasonable terms. He must not only sell what he deals in somewhat cheaper, but, in order to get it to sell, he must sometimes, too, buy it dearer. The demand for productive labour, by the increase of the funds which are destined for maintaining it, grows every day greater and greater. Labourers easily find employment; but the owners of capitals find it difficult to get labourers to employ. Their competition raises the wages of labour, and sinks the profits of stock. But when the profits which can be made by the use of a capital are in this manner diminished, as it were, at both ends, the price which can be paid for the use of it, that is, the rate of interest, must necessarily be diminished with them.
p7.zh: 随着利息借出股票的数量增加,利息或因使用股票而必须支付的价格必然会减少,不仅会减少那些使物品的市场价格随着数量增加而普遍下降的一般原因,而且会减少与本案特殊原因有关的其他原因。 随着任何国家首都的增加,通过使用这些资本而获得的利润必然减少。在国内找到一种利用任何新资本的有利可图的方法变得越来越困难。 因此,在不同首都之间产生了竞争,其中一个首都的主人试图获得另一个首都所占据的这一职业;但是,在大多数情况下,他可以希望以其他任何手段,只有以更合理的条件,才能使另一个首都摆脱这一职业。 他不仅要卖掉他交易的便宜点,而且为了让这些东西卖掉,他有时还必须买到更亲爱的东西。 对生产性劳动力的需求,由于用于维持生产性劳动力的资金的增加,每天都在增加。劳工很容易找到工作;但首都的业主发现很难雇用劳工。 他们的竞争提高了劳动力的工资,并吸收了股票的利润。 但是,当通过使用资本而能够取得的利润以这种方式减少时,如同在两端一样,可以用资本支付的价格,即利率,必然会随着资本减少而降低。

p8.original: Mr Locke, Mr Lawe, and Mr Montesquieu, as well as many other writers, seem to have imagined that the increase of the quantity of gold and silver, in consequence of the discovery of the Spanish West Indies, was the real cause of the lowering of the rate of interest through the greater part of Europe. Those metals, they say, having become of less value themselves, the use of any particular portion of them necessarily became of less value too, and, consequently, the price which could be paid for it. This notion, which at first sight seems so plausible, has been so fully exposed by Mr Hume, that it is, perhaps, unnecessary to say any thing more about it. The following very short and plain argument, however, may serve to explain more distinctly the fallacy which seems to have misled those gentlemen.
p8.zh: 洛克先生、劳先生和蒙特斯基厄先生以及其他许多作家似乎都认为,由于发现西印度群岛,黄金和白银数量的增加是欧洲大部分地区利率下降的真正原因。 他们说,这些金属由于本身的价值越来越小,使用其中任何一部分也必然变得价值较低,因此,可能为此付出的代价也就越少。这一概念乍看看来是可信的,但休姆先生已充分揭示了这一点,也许没有必要再多谈这个问题。 然而,以下非常简短和明确的论点可能更清楚地解释似乎误导这些先生们的谬误。

p9.original: Before the discovery of the Spanish West Indies, ten per cent. seems to have been the common rate of interest through the greater part of Europe. It has since that time, in different countries, sunk to six, five, four, and three per cent. Let us suppose, that in every particular country the value of silver has sunk precisely in the same proportion as the rate of interest; and that in those countries, for example, where interest has been reduced from ten to five per cent. the same quantity of silver can now purchase just half the quantity of goods which it could have purchased before. This supposition will not, I believe, be found anywhere agreeable to the truth; but it is the most favourable to the opinion which we are going to examine; and, even upon this supposition, it is utterly impossible that the lowering of the value of silver could have the smallest tendency to lower the rate of interest. If £100 are in those countries now of no more value than £50 were then, £10 must now be of no more value than £5 were then. Whatever were the causes which lowered the value of the capital, the same must necessarily have lowered that of the interest, and exactly in the same proportion. The proportion between the value of the capital and that of the interest must have remained the same, though the rate had never been altered. By altering the rate, on the contrary, the proportion between those two values is necessarily altered. If £100 now are worth no more than £50 were then, £5 now can be worth no more than £2:10s. were then. By reducing the rate of interest, therefore, from ten to five per cent. we give for the use of a capital, which is supposed to be equal to one half of its former value, an interest which is equal to one fourth only of the value of the former interest.
p9.zh: 在西班牙西印度群岛发现之前,10%的利率似乎是通过欧洲大部的共同利率. 从那时起,在不同国家,它沉没到六、五、四和3%。 让我们假设,在每一个特定国家,银子的价值已经沉没在与利率完全相同的比例上;例如,在那些利息从10%降至5%的国家,同样数量的银子现在只能购买它以前本来可以购买的商品的一半。 我认为,在任何符合真理的地方都不会找到这种假设;但它最有利于我们将要审查的意见;即使根据这种假设,降低银的价值完全不可能有降低利率的最小趋势。 如果100英镑在那些现在价值不超过50英镑的国家,那么10英镑现在必须不超过当时的5英镑. 无论降低资本价值的原因是什么,都必然会降低利益,而且比例也完全相同。资本价值与利息价值的比例必须保持不变,尽管利率从未改变。 相反,通过改变比率,这两个数值之间的比例必然会改变。 如果现在100英镑的价值不超过50英镑,那么现在5英镑的价值可能不超过2:10.当时. 因此,通过将利率从10%降低到5%,我们给予一笔资本的使用权,这笔资本应等于其以前价值的一半,利息只等于以前利息价值的四分之一。

p10.original: An increase in the quantity of silver, while that of the commodities circulated by means of it remained the same, could have no other effect than to diminish the value of that metal. The nominal value of all sorts of goods would be greater, but their real value would be precisely the same as before. They would be exchanged for a greater number of pieces of silver; but the quantity of labour which they could command, the number of people whom they could maintain and employ, would be precisely the same. The capital of the country would be the same, though a greater number of pieces might be requisite for conveying any equal portion of it from one hand to another. The deeds of assignment, like the conveyances of a verbose attorney, would be more cumbersome; but the thing assigned would be precisely the same as before, and could produce only the same effects. The funds for maintaining productive labour being the same, the demand for it would be the same. Its price or wages, therefore, though nominally greater, would really be the same. They would be paid in a greater number of pieces of silver, but they would purchase only the same quantity of goods. The profits of stock would be the same, both nominally and really. The wages of labour are commonly computed by the quantity of silver which is paid to the labourer. When that is increased, therefore, his wages appear to be increased, though they may sometimes be no greater than before. But the profits of stock are not computed by the number of pieces of silver with which they are paid, but by the proportion which those pieces bear to the whole capital employed. Thus, in a particular country, 5s. a-week are said to be the common wages of labour, and ten per cent. the common profits of stock; but the whole capital of the country being the same as before, the competition between the different capitals of individuals into which it was divided would likewise be the same. They would all trade with the same advantages and disadvantages. The common proportion between capital and profit, therefore, would be the same, and consequently the common interest of money; what can commonly be given for the use of money being necessarily regulated by what can commonly be made by the use of it.
p10.zh: 增加银子的数量,而通过银子流通的商品的数量保持不变,除了降低这种金属的价值之外,没有其他效果。 所有各类商品的名义价值将更高,但其实际价值与以前完全相同。 他们将换取更多的白银;但他们可以指挥的劳动力数量,他们可以维持和雇用的人数,将完全相同。国家的首都是相同的,尽管为了将其中任何同等部分从一手传递给另一手,可能需要更多的块。转让契约与动词律师的传递方式一样,将更为繁琐;但所转让的东西与以前完全相同,只能产生同样的效果。维持生产性劳动的资金是相同的,对它的需求是相同的。 因此,其价格或工资虽然名义上更高,但实际上是一样的。 他们将用更多的白银支付,但他们只购买同样数量的货物。股票的利润无论名义上还是实际上都是一样的。劳工工资通常按支付给工人的银子数量计算。 因此,当工资增加时,他的工资似乎增加,尽管有时可能不会比以前多。 但是,股票的利润不是按所付的银块数量计算的,而是按这些银块与所雇用的全部资本的比例计算的。 因此,在某个国家,每周5s据说是劳动力的共同工资,10%是股票的共同利润;但是,全国的首都与以前一样,被划分为不同首都的个人之间的竞争同样是相同的。 它们都将以同样的利弊进行贸易。 因此,资本和利润之间的共同比例是一样的,因此也是金钱的共同利益;通常可以给予资金的使用,但必须受到资金使用通常可以提供的资金的制约。

p11.original: Any increase in the quantity of commodities annually circulated within the country, while that of the money which circulated them remained the same, would, on the contrary, produce many other important effects, besides that of raising the value of the money. The capital of the country, though it might nominally be the same, would really be augmented. It might continue to be expressed by the same quantity of money, but it would command a greater quantity of labour. The quantity of productive labour which it could maintain and employ would be increased, and consequently the demand for that labour. Its wages would naturally rise with the demand, and yet might appear to sink. They might be paid with a smaller quantity of money, but that smaller quantity might purchase a greater quantity of goods than a greater had done before. The profits of stock would be diminished, both really and in appearance. The whole capital of the country being augmented, the competition between the different capitals of which it was composed would naturally be augmented along with it. The owners of those particular capitals would be obliged to content themselves with a smaller proportion of the produce of that labour which their respective capitals employed. The interest of money, keeping pace always with the profits of stock, might, in this manner, be greatly diminished, though the value of money, or the quantity of goods which any particular sum could purchase, was greatly augmented.
p11.zh: 每年在国内流通的商品数量的任何增加,而流通的商品数量保持不变,相反,除了提高货币价值之外,还将产生许多其他重要影响。 该国首都虽然名义上可能相同,但确实会扩大。 它可能继续用同样数量的资金来表示,但它会得到更多的劳动力。 它能够维持和雇用的生产性劳动力的数量将增加,从而增加对该劳动力的需求。其工资自然会随着需求而增加,但似乎会下降。付款方式可能较少,但数量较少的购买货物数量可能比以前多。股票的利润将会减少,无论是真的还是表面上。整个国家的首都正在扩大,它所组成的不同首都之间的竞争自然也会随之增加。 这些特定首都的所有人必须满足于各自首都所雇用的这种劳动力的一小部分。金钱的利得总是与股票的利润保持同步,这种方式可能会大大降低,尽管金钱的价值或任何特定数额可以购买的货物的数量都大大增加。

p12.original: In some countries the interest of money has been prohibited by law. But as something can everywhere be made by the use of money, something ought everywhere to be paid for the use of it. This regulation, instead of preventing, has been found from experience to increase the evil of usury. The debtor being obliged to pay, not only for the use of the money, but for the risk which his creditor runs by accepting a compensation for that use, he is obliged, if one may say so, to insure his creditor from the penalties of usury.
p12.zh: 在一些国家,法律禁止金钱利益。 但是,由于钱的使用可以使任何地方有所作为,所以应该向任何地方支付钱的使用费。 这一规定不是预防的,而是从经验中发现的,增加了高利贷的罪恶.债务人有义务付款,这不仅是为了使用这笔钱,也是为了其债权人通过接受对这笔资金的补偿而承担的风险,如果有人这样说,他有义务为其债权人提供利息的处罚。

p13.original: In countries where interest is permitted, the law in order to prevent the extortion of usury, generally fixes the highest rate which can be taken without incurring a penalty. This rate ought always to be somewhat above the lowest market price, or the price which is commonly paid for the use of money by those who can give the most undoubted security. If this legal rate should be fixed below the lowest market rate, the effects of this fixation must be nearly the same as those of a total prohibition of interest. The creditor will not lend his money for less than the use of it is worth, and the debtor must pay him for the risk which he runs by accepting the full value of that use. If it is fixed precisely at the lowest market price, it ruins, with honest people who respect the laws of their country, the credit of all those who cannot give the very best security, and obliges them to have recourse to exorbitant usurers. In a country such as Great Britain, where money is lent to government at three per cent. and to private people, upon good security, at four and four and a-half, the present legal rate, five per cent. is perhaps as proper as any.
p13.zh: 在允许利息的国家,法律为防止高利贷的勒索,一般规定最高利率,而无需处罚。 这种利率应始终略高于最低市场价格,或通常由那些可以提供最无可置疑的担保的人为使用货币而支付的价格。 如果将这一法定利率固定在低于最低市场利率的水平,这种固定利率的影响必须几乎与完全禁止利息的影响相同。债权人将不以低于其价值的用途而借出其资金,债务人必须通过接受该用途的全部价值来支付其经营的风险。 如果它完全固定在最低的市场价格上,它就会破坏诚实的人们,他们尊重他们国家的法律,是所有那些不能提供最优保障的人的功劳,并迫使他们求助于高利贷者。 在大不列颠这样的国家,政府获得3%的贷款,私人获得良好安全,以4和4个半的利率获得目前法定的5%贷款,这也许与任何贷款一样适当。

p14.original: The legal rate, it is to be observed, though it ought to be somewhat above, ought not to be much above the lowest market rate. If the legal rate of interest in Great Britain, for example, was fixed so high as eight or ten per cent. the greater part of the money which was to be lent, would be lent to prodigals and projectors, who alone would be willing to give this high interest. Sober people, who will give for the use of money no more than a part of what they are likely to make by the use of it, would not venture into the competition. A great part of the capital of the country would thus be kept out of the hands which were most likely to make a profitable and advantageous use of it, and thrown into those which were most likely to waste and destroy it. Where the legal rate of interest, on the contrary, is fixed but a very little above the lowest market rate, sober people are universally preferred, as borrowers, to prodigals and projectors. The person who lends money gets nearly as much interest from the former as he dares to take from the latter, and his money is much safer in the hands of the one set of people than in those of the other. A great part of the capital of the country is thus thrown into the hands in which it is most likely to be employed with advantage.
p14.zh: 应该注意到,虽然法定利率应该略高于,但不应大大高于最低市场利率。 例如,如果英国的法定利率定得高达8%或10%。 拟借出的大部分资金将借给浪人和投影者,只有他们愿意给予这种高息。索伯人为了金钱的用途而付出的,不过是他们通过使用金钱而可能付出的部分,他们不会冒险参与竞争. 因此,该国很大一部分首都将被排除在最有可能获利和有利地使用首都的手中,并被扔到最有可能浪费和摧毁首都的手中。 相反,如果法定利率固定,但略高于最低的市场利率,那么作为借款人,清醒的人普遍倾向于浪子和投影者。借钱的人从前者那里得到的利息几乎与他敢从后者那里得到的一样多,而他的钱在一对人的手中比在另一对人的手中要安全得多. 因此,该国首都的很大一部分被投入到最有可能以有利条件加以利用的手中。

p15.original: No law can reduce the common rate of interest below the lowest ordinary market rate at the time when that law is made. Notwithstanding the edict of 1766, by which the French king attempted to reduce the rate of interest from five to four per cent. money continued to be lent in France at five per cent. the law being evaded in several different ways.
p15.zh: 任何法律都不能将共同利率降低到制定该法律时最低的普通市场利率以下。 尽管1766年的法令,法国国王试图将利率从5%降低到4%,但法国继续以5%的利率借贷,法律以几种不同的方式被规避.

p16.original: The ordinary market price of land, it is to be observed, depends everywhere upon the ordinary market rate of interest. The person who has a capital from which he wishes to derive a revenue, without taking the trouble to employ it himself, deliberates whether he should buy land with it, or lend it out at interest. The superior security of land, together with some other advantages which almost everywhere attend upon this species of property, will generally dispose him to content himself with a smaller revenue from land, than what he might have by lending out his money at interest. These advantages are sufficient to compensate a certain difference of revenue; but they will compensate a certain difference only; and if the rent of land should fall short of the interest of money by a greater difference, nobody would buy land, which would soon reduce its ordinary price. On the contrary, if the advantages should much more than compensate the difference, everybody would buy land, which again would soon raise its ordinary price. When interest was at ten per cent. land was commonly sold for ten or twelve years purchase. As interest sunk to six, five, and four per cent. the price of land rose to twenty, five-and-twenty, and thirty years purchase. The market rate of interest is higher in France than in England, and the common price of land is lower. In England it commonly sells at thirty, in France at twenty years purchase.
p16.zh: 土地的正常市场价格,应当观察,取决于各地的正常市场利率.拥有资本,希望从中获得收入的人,不费力地自己雇人,考虑用资本购买土地,还是以利息出借土地。土地的优越安全,加上几乎到处都有的其他一些好处,一般会使他自己从土地中获得的收入比他借出利息所得的收入要少。 这些优势足以补偿一定的收入差额;但是它们只能补偿一定的差额;如果土地的租金以较大的差额低于金钱的利息,那么没有人会买土地,这很快会降低土地的普通价格. 相反,如果好处远远不止于补偿差额,每个人都会购买土地,这很快将再次提高土地的普通价格。 当利息为10%时,通常出售土地10年或12年。利息跌至六,五,四个百分点,地价涨至二十,五,二十,三十年购地. 法国的市场利率高于英国,土地的共同价格更低. 在英国,它通常以30岁的价格销售,在法国则以20年的价格购买。
